[[[1]]()]() These lists are maintained and updated by specialized organizations like the Gerontology Research Group (GRG), a volunteer-led entity dedicated to validating extreme ages via a multi-step process involving archival research and cross-referencing of historical records, and LongeviQuest, which employs similar documentary standards to certify claims and track global longevity records. [[[2]]()]() Such validations are essential due to the rarity of supercentenarians—over 3,000 have been validated worldwide, with approximately 230 living as of November 2025—and the challenges of age verification at advanced ages, where errors in reporting can occur without strict scrutiny. [[[3]]()]() [[[4]]()]() As of November 17, 2025, the verified oldest living person is Ethel Caterham, a British woman born on August 21, 1909, who turned 116 years old in August 2025 and holds the Guinness World Records title for oldest living person.

...

[[[23]]()]() As of November 2025, approximately 314 living supercentenarians have achieved full validation through these processes. [[[25]]()]()

## Oldest Living Supercentenarians Worldwide

### Ranked List of Verified Individuals

This section presents the ranked list of the world's oldest verified living supercentenarians, defined as individuals aged 110 years or older whose ages have been rigorously validated by reputable organizations such as the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) or LongeviQuest. [[[9]]()]() [[[26]]()]() Inclusion is limited to cases with full validation to the supercentenarian threshold, excluding any pending, unverified, or disputed claims to ensure accuracy and reliability. [[[9]]()]() [[[26]]()]() As of December 12, 2025, only one verified individual exceeds 116 years, highlighting the extreme rarity of such longevity , with approximately 314 validated living supercentenarians worldwide in total.

...

The United Kingdom maintains a prominent position in global longevity records, with Ethel Caterham, born on 21 August 1909 in Shipton Bellinger, Hampshire , recognized as the world's oldest verified living person at 116 years old as of November 2025. [[[5]]()]() [[[57]]()]() Her age was validated by LongeviQuest in April 2025, surpassing previous British records and confirming her as the longest-lived person ever from the UK. [[[18]]()]() This milestone underscores the UK's robust archival systems, including parish records predating the Civil Registration Act of 1837 and subsequent birth certificates, which facilitate thorough age verification for supercentenarians . Age validation in the UK benefits from centralized records maintained by the General Register Office since 1837, enabling organizations like LongeviQuest and the Gerontology Research Group to cross-reference documents such as baptismal entries, census data, and death certificates of relatives for pre-20th-century births.

...

In Spain , Carme Noguera Falguera, born 22 August 1914 in Olot , Girona , is the doyenne at 111 years and 87 days as of November 17, 2025, validated through civil and church documents. Recent validations in Spain have benefited from improved archival access, though the country has seen fewer supercentenarians following the death of Maria Branyas Morera in 2024 at 117 and Angelina Torres Vallbona in 2025 at 112.

### South America

Brazil leads the region with verified cases amid challenges from incomplete early 20th-century records and frequent unverified claims. The oldest living person is Yolanda Beltrão de Azevedo, a female born 13 January 1911 in João Pessoa, Paraíba, aged 114 years, 308 days as of November 17, 2025, validated by GRG. The world's oldest validated living man, João Marinho Neto, born 5 October 1912 in João Pessoa, Brazil , is 113 years and 43 days old; he attributes his health to faith and family.

Supercentenarians that are categorized as "pending validation" have their ages partially authenticated, but remain to be fully processed by an age validation organization. The last group, "unvalidated", refers to supercentenarians that have not had their ages authenticated but for whom there is sufficient reliable-source reporting to at least have a claimed date of birth. However, only claimants age 110–114 that could potentially be validated in the future are included here, although exaggerated claims 115-129 can be found at Living longevity claims , and those false claims above 130 can be found at Living longevity myths .

Since the death of 116-year-old Inah Canabarro Lucas of Brazil on 30 April 2025, 116-year-old Ethel Caterham of the UK is the oldest living person whose age is validated.

# List of the verified oldest people

Ara Eve Leo Sal

1x

The list of the verified oldest people documents supercentenarians—individuals who have lived to 110 years or more—whose ages have been rigorously authenticated through primary documents and expert validation by organizations such as the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) and Guinness World Records . [[[1]]()]() [[[2]]()]() These validations typically require birth certificates, census records, and other contemporaneous evidence to confirm longevity claims , distinguishing verified cases from unproven assertions of extreme age.
[[[3]]()]() The list encompasses both historical figures and currently living individuals, highlighting human longevity extremes and serving as a key resource for gerontological research. [[[4]]()]() The record for the longest verified human lifespan belongs to Jeanne Calment of France , who lived 122 years and 164 days, from February 21, 1875, to August 4, 1997; her age was authenticated by multiple independent researchers using French civil and church records. [[[2]]()]() [[[3]]()]() Among men, the oldest verified is Jiroemon Kimura of Japan , who reached 116 years and 54 days before his death on June 12, 2013. As of November 14, 2025, Ethel Caterham of the United Kingdom holds the title of oldest living verified person at 116 years, 85 days (born August 21, 1909), following the death of previous titleholder Inah Canabarro Lucas on April 30, 2025. [[[4]]()]() [[[5]]()]() The oldest verified living man is João Marinho Neto of Brazil , aged 113 years, 40 days (born October 5, 1912).

## Current Oldest Living People

### Oldest Living Woman

As of November 14, 2025, Ethel May Caterham (née Collins), born on August 21, 1909, in Shipton Bellinger, Hampshire , England , holds the title of the world's oldest verified living woman at 116 years and 85 days old. [[[18]]()]() She resides in a care home in Lightwater, Surrey , United Kingdom , and remains in good health for her age, having outlived her husband and both daughters. [[[19]]()]() Her age has been rigorously validated by the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) through primary documents including her birth certificate , census records, and baptismal entries, confirming her as a supercentenarian since 2019. [[[18]]()]() Caterham's life spans major historical events, including both World Wars; she was a child during World War I and worked as an au pair for a military family in Germany during the interwar period .

...

[[[23]]()]() Women have historically dominated these records, comprising over 90% of validated supercentenarians , largely due to biological advantages such as the protective effects of estrogen on cardiovascular health , which contribute to women outliving men by an average of 5 to 7 years globally. [[[24]]()]() [[[25]]()]()

### Oldest Living Man

The oldest verified living man is João Marinho Neto, born on 5 October 1912 in Maranguape, Ceará , Brazil , who is 113 years and 40 days old as of 14 November 2025. [[[26]]()]() [[[27]]()]() He currently resides in Apuiarés, Ceará , Brazil , and remains alive, surrounded by family. [[[28]]()]() Neto's age has been validated by the Gerontology Research Group (GRG) and LongeviQuest, recognized organizations in supercentenarian verification, based on birth records and supporting family documentation.

...

[[[4]]()]() [[[32]]()]() Male supercentenarians represent only about 10% of all verified cases aged 110 or older, a disparity largely due to higher male mortality rates in earlier life stages from factors such as occupational risks and behavioral patterns. [[[33]]()]() [[[34]]()]() Among those who reach extreme old age, lifestyle elements like balanced diets and regular physical activity—such as Neto's lifelong farming—appear to play a key role in sustaining health, often outweighing purely biological differences in verified long-lived men. [[[35]]()]() This rarity underscores the exceptional nature of male supercentenarians, with fewer than 30 validated living examples worldwide as of late 2025. [[[6]]()]()

Sister Andre, Lucile Randon in the registry of birth, the eldest French and European citizen, prays in a wheelchair, on the eve of her 117th birthday Photo credit: Getty Toby Saunders Published: August 28, 2025 at 1:34 pm * * * The verifiably oldest ever person in the world is **Jeanne Louise Calment** , who lived to the age of 122 years and 164 days old.

It’s incredible to imagine what Calment and today's supercentenarians (people who are 110 years old or older) have witnessed in their lifetimes.

...

With different cultural, hygienic, and scientific reasons, average life expectancy around the world changes depending on which country you live in and even where in that country you live.

The UN estimates that the worldwide life expectancy is now [73\.3 years](https://desapublications.un.org/publications/world-population-prospects-2024-summary-results?_gl=1*wckui1*_ga*NDM0NjMxMjY4LjE3NTM3Nzg5NTA.*_ga_TK9BQL5X7Z*czE3NTYyOTc2ODIkbzMkZzAkdDE3NTYyOTc2ODIkajYwJGwwJGgw) – that's about nine years longer than people lived in 1995.

## Who is the oldest person alive today?

The oldest living person as of August 2025 is Ethel Caterham. She is 116 years old.

She was born on 21 August 1909 in Hampshire, UK, during the reign of Edward VII. She currently lives in a nursing home in Lightwater, Surrey.

According to the [Guinness World Records](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.
com/news/2025/5/uks-oldest-ever-person-ethel-caterham-becomes-worlds-oldest-person-at-age-115) , she was the second of eight children. Remarkably, her older sister Gladys Babilas also made it past the 100 mark, living to 104 years and 78 days.

Her husband, whom she first met back in 1931, died in 1976, leaving behind his classic Triumph Dolomite car, which she still drove until the age of 97. Tragically, she also outlived both of her children.

## Previous title holders

### Jeanne Louise Calment - Oldest person ever

Jeanne Calment 120-year-old Jeanne Louise Calment sitting in armchair at home © Ian Cook/Getty Images

Jeanne Louise Calment is the oldest verified person to have ever lived. The Frenchwoman lived to the ripe old age of 122 years and 164 days old. She was born on 21 February 1875 and passed away aged 122 on 4 August 1997.

According to [Guinness World Records](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.
com/world-records/oldest-person) , Calment “ate almost 1kg of chocolate” every week, and smoked “from the age of 21 and only quit when she was 117.” She also “sold painting canvasses to Van Gogh,” whom she described as “ugly as sin” with a “vile temper and smelled of booze.”

### Jiroemon Kimura - Oldest man ever

Jiroemon Kimura, the former world's oldest man. At the time of his death, Jiroemon Kimura had 7 children, 14 grandchildren, 25 great-grandchildren and 14 great-great-grandchildren - Photo credit: Getty

Jiroemon Kimura lived to be 116 years and 54 days old. The Japanese supercentenarian was born on 19 April 1897 and lived through to 12 June 2013. The Guinness World Records [quotes him as saying](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/oldest-person-\(male\)) “eat light to live long” and states that he continued to engage in agriculture until he was 90.

### Lucile Randon - 118
Another Frenchwoman, Lucile Randon (see main picture) lived to the age of 118 years and 340 days old. Born on 11 February 1904, she passed away on 17 January 2023.

### Kane Tanaka - 119

Born on 2 January 1903 and passing away on 19 April 2022, the Japanese woman lived to be 119 years and 107 days old.

### Chiyo Miyako - 117

Another Japanese woman, Chiyo Miyako was born on 2 May 1901 and died on 22 July 2018, living up to the ripe age of 117 years and 81 days old.

### Nabi Tajima - 117

Nabi Tajima 117-year-old Nabi Tajima © JIJI PRESS/AFP via Getty Images

Yet another Japanese supercentenarian, Nabi Tajima lived to be 117 years and 260 days old, from her birth on 4 August 1900 to her death on 21 April 2018.

### Violet Brown - 117

We head to Jamaica next and to Violet Brown. She lived to be 117 years and 189 days old. She was born on 10 March 1900 and passed away on 15 September 2017.

### Emma Martina Luigia Morano - 117
Emma Morano Emma Morano in 2016 © OLIVIER MORIN/AFP via Getty Images

Next is Emma Martina Luigia Morano. The Italian supercentenarian also lived to be 117 years old (plus 137 days) and was born on 29 November 1899 before her death on 15 April 2017.

### María Branyas Morera - 117

When María Branyas Morera died aged 117 in August 2024 aged 117 years 168 days, she was the eighth-oldest person (with a verifiable age) in history.

She was born on 4th March 1907 in San Francisco, California, and lived in Texas and New Orleans before her Spanish family returned to Catalonia during World War I, according to [Guinness World Records](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2024/8/worlds-oldest-person-maria-branyas-morera-dies-aged-117) .

She said she lived “an orderly life that is socially very pleasant… a good life, without excesses.”

### Susannah Mushatt Jones - 116

Next up we have Susannah Mushatt Jones from the USA.
She lived to be 116 years and 311 days old and was born on 6 July 1899 and died on 12 May 2016.

### Jeralean Talley - 116

World's former oldest person Jeralean Talley in 2015. World's former oldest person Jeralean Talley in 2015 - Photo credit: Getty

Finally, we have Jeralean Talley, who was also from the USA. She lived to be 116 years and 25 days old. She was born on 23 May 1899 and passed away on 17 June 2015.
